newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government bonds end higher on interbank.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government bonds end higher on interbank.

text.p: Singapore government bond prices ended higher in moderate trade on Tuesday on retail and interbank interest, dealers said.
"Bond prices were marked up slightly today following a small fall in the interbank rate. Treasury bill yields were slightly lower. Volume was moderate," a local dealer said.
Among bonds, April 1999 ended at S$98.48/98.53 compared with Monday's close of S$98.38/98.43, May 2002 at S$99.45/99.50 against S$99.38/99.43 and June 2003 at S$94.50/94.55 from S$94.38/94.43.
The overnight interbank offered rate slipped to 2 1-7/8 percent versus Monday's 2-3/8 2-1/4 percent.
In treasury bills, three-months closed at a yield of 2.65/2.60 percent against Monday's yield of 2.85/2.80 percent and one-year at a yield of 2.70/2.65 percent from 2.80/2.75 percent.
